hook: The Florentine who wrote The Prince, a ruthless rulebook for rulers.

pages.x: Niccolò Machiavelli was born in Florence in 1469. When the Medici were driven out and Florence became a republic, he rose to be one of its top officials, handling its dealings with other states and setting up a citizen army.

As an envoy he met kings and popes, and watched Cesare Borgia, the pope's ruthless son, carve out a state in central Italy. Borgia invited his rebellious captains to make peace, then had them strangled. Machiavelli admired his nerve.

When the Medici came back in 1512, Machiavelli was sacked, accused of plotting, and tortured, hung by his wrists from a rope. He confessed nothing, was released, and retired to his small farm outside Florence.

In a famous letter he describes his evenings on the farm. He takes off his muddy clothes, puts on robes fit for a court, and enters his study to talk with the great men of the past in their books, for four hours forgetting every trouble.

There he wrote The Prince, a handbook for rulers. It said a prince must sometimes be cruel to keep the peace, that it is safer to be feared than loved, and that a ruler must be a fox to spot traps and a lion to scare off wolves.

Machiavelli was the first to write about politics as it really works, not as it ought to. "Machiavellian" now means cunning and ruthless, but he is also called the founder of modern political science.
pts: A founder of modern political thought
His name became a word for ruthless cunning
